title: Dasakam 95 — Dhyānayogaḥ – Mokṣaprāptimārgaḥ
description: The movement from the guṇas and transient pursuits toward bhakti, disciplined meditation, contemplation of Bhagavan’s form, and single-minded refuge.
translation_note: No vetted English stanza translation is present in the supplied source bundle; translation_en is intentionally empty pending editorial review.

stanzas.sanskrit:
आदौ हैरण्यगर्भीं तनुमविकलजीवात्मिकामास्थितस्त्वं
जीवत्वं प्राप्य मायागुणगणखचितो वर्तसे विश्वयोने ।
तत्रोद्वृद्धेन सत्त्वेन तु गुणयुगलं भक्तिभावं गतेन
छित्वा सत्त्वं च हित्वा पुनरनुपहितो वर्तिताहे त्वमेव ॥ ९५-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: In the beginning Bhagwan were in an undivided state of all jivas in the Hiranyagarbha form. Then Bhagwan became took up multiplicity of jivas, and become associated with Maayaa and its various Gunas. With the well developed and dominant Sattva, devotional attitude is reached, by which the other two gunas Rajas and Tamas are destroyed. Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to be granted this state of Nirguna, so that he can become completely like Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ādau hairaṇyagarbhīṃ tanumavikalajīvātmikāmāsthitastvaṃ
jīvatvaṃ prāpya māyāguṇagaṇakhacito vartase viśvayone |
tatrodvṛddhena sattvena tu guṇayugalaṃ bhaktibhāvaṃ gatena
chitvā sattvaṃ ca hitvā punaranupahito vartitāhe tvameva || 95-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सत्त्वोन्मेषात् कदाचित् खलु विषयरसे दोषबोधेऽपि भूमन्
भूयोऽप्येषु प्रवृत्तिः सतमसि रजसि प्रोद्धते दुर्निवारा ।
चित्तं तावद्गुणाश्च ग्रथितमिह मिथस्तानि सर्वाणि रोद्धुं
तुर्ये त्वय्येकभक्तिः शरणमिति भवान् हंसरूपी न्यगादीत् ॥ ९५-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When the Sattva Guna predominates, the harmfulness of sense enjoyments is realised. Whereas when the Rajas and Tamas are predominant, to detach from worldly enjoyments becomes difficult, because the mind and the gunas are mutually interlinked. Bhagwan the form of Swan advised that only way to be focused towards the path of mukthi is to keeps the mind and soul fixed on Bhagwan who is Nirguna by nature.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sattvonmeṣāt kadācit khalu viṣayarase doṣabodhe’pi bhūman
bhūyo’pyeṣu pravṛttiḥ satamasi rajasi proddhate durnivārā |
cittaṃ tāvadguṇāśca grathitamiha mithastāni sarvāṇi roddhuṃ
turye tvayyekabhaktiḥ śaraṇamiti bhavān haṃsarūpī nyagādīt || 95-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सन्ति श्रेयांसि भूयांस्यपि रुचिभिदया कर्मिणां निर्मितानि
क्षुद्रानन्दाश्च सान्ता बहुविधगतयः कृष्ण तेभ्यो भवेयुः ।
त्वं चाचख्याथ सख्ये ननु महिततमां श्रेयसां भक्तिमेकां
त्वद्भक्त्यानन्दतुल्यः खलु विषयजुषां सम्मदः केन वा स्यात् ॥ ९५-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: There are many paths of welfare suitable for varying tastes of people as means of fulfilment. But they are all only temporary and trivial pleasures. Bhagwan  describes to HIS friend, Uddhava, that devotion is the most glorious path for attainment of moksha. The bliss experienced through devotion to Bhagwan, is no comparison to those who enjoy just worldly benefits.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
santi śreyāṃsi bhūyāṃsyapi rucibhidayā karmiṇāṃ nirmitāni
kṣudrānandāśca sāntā bahuvidhagatayaḥ kṛṣṇa tebhyo bhaveyuḥ |
tvaṃ cācakhyātha sakhye nanu mahitatamāṃ śreyasāṃ bhaktimekāṃ
tvadbhaktyānandatulyaḥ khalu viṣayajuṣāṃ sammadaḥ kena vā syāt || 95-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्भक्त्या तुष्टबुद्धेः सुखमिह चरतो विच्युताशस्य चाशाः
सर्वाः स्युः सौख्यमय्यः सलिलकुहरगस्येव तोयैकमय्यः ।
सोऽयं खल्विन्द्रलोकं कमलजभवनं योगसिद्धीश्च हृद्याः
नाकाङ्क्षत्येतदास्तां स्वयमनुपतिते मोक्षसौख्येऽप्यनीहः ॥ ९५-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: A person whose mind is satisfied in devotion, moves about happily in this world. The person who has dropped all desires, finds every place full of joy, just like an aquatic creature living in deep waters which finds water everywhere. He does not prefer brahmaloka, satyaloka or yogic powers or even moksha which is bestowed upon him automatically.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadbhaktyā tuṣṭabuddheḥ sukhamiha carato vicyutāśasya cāśāḥ
sarvāḥ syuḥ saukhyamayyaḥ salilakuharagasyeva toyaikamayyaḥ |
so’yaṃ khalvindralokaṃ kamalajabhavanaṃ yogasiddhīśca hṛdyāḥ
nākāṅkṣatyetadāstāṃ svayamanupatite mokṣasaukhye’pyanīhaḥ || 95-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वद्भक्तो बाध्यमानोऽपि च विषयरसैरिन्द्रियाशान्तिहेतो-
-र्भक्त्यैवाक्रम्यमाणैः पुनरपि खलु तैर्दुर्बलैर्नाभिजय्यः ।
सप्तार्चिर्दीपितार्चिर्दहति किल यथा भूरिदारुप्रपञ्चं
त्वद्भक्त्यौघे तथैव प्रदहति दुरितं दुर्मदः क्वेन्द्रियाणाम् ॥ ९५-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Sometimes it is difficult to win over and control the sense organs of the body but due to repeated involvement in devotion to Bhagwan, the pleasures attainable due to bodily urges are weakened and finally lost. Just as the fire burns any log put in to it, devotion to Bhagwan can remove any sin and suppresses the domination by bodily senses completely.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadbhakto bādhyamāno’pi ca viṣayarasairindriyāśāntiheto-
-rbhaktyaivākramyamāṇaiḥ punarapi khalu tairdurbalairnābhijayyaḥ |
saptārcirdīpitārcirdahati kila yathā bhūridāruprapañcaṃ
tvadbhaktyaughe tathaiva pradahati duritaṃ durmadaḥ kvendriyāṇām || 95-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
चित्तार्द्रीभावमुच्चैर्वपुषि च पुलकं हर्षबाष्पं च हित्वा
चित्तं शुद्ध्येत्कथं वा किमु बहुतपसा विद्यया वीतभक्तेः ।
त्वद्गाथास्वादसिद्धाञ्जनसततमरीमृज्यमानोऽयमात्मा
चक्षुर्वत् तत्त्वसूक्ष्मं भजति न तु तथाभ्यस्तया तर्ककोट्या ॥ ९५-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One's mind and heart melts and gets purified due to experiencing tears, goosebumps with devotion to Bhagwan. One who has no devotion in his heart, gains nothing by penances and attainment of knowledge. Only by enjoying the pastimes of Bhagwan,  mind and soul gets purified and attains tattva gnanam.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
cittārdrībhāvamuccairvapuṣi ca pulakaṃ harṣabāṣpaṃ ca hitvā
cittaṃ śuddhyetkathaṃ vā kimu bahutapasā vidyayā vītabhakteḥ |
tvadgāthāsvādasiddhāñjanasatatamarīmṛjyamāno’yamātmā
cakṣurvat tattvasūkṣmaṃ bhajati na tu tathābhyastayā tarkakoṭyā || 95-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
ध्यानम् ते शीलयेयं समतनुसुखबद्धासनो नासिकाग्र-
-न्यस्ताक्षः पूरकाद्यैर्जितपवनपथश्चित्तपद्मं त्ववाञ्चम् ।
ऊर्ध्वाग्रं भावयित्वा रविविधुशिखिनः संविचिन्त्योपरिष्टात्
तत्रस्थं भावये त्वां सजलजलधरश्यामलं कोमलाङ्गम् ॥ ९५-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri explains about meditation that one has to sit erect in a comfortable pose (sukhaasana) and gaze on the tip of the nose in between the two eyebrows and regulate the breath energies through Pranayama. While doing this, one should imagine the downward lotus in the heart as facing upward and imagine the sun, moon and fire above it and Bhagwan in a delicate dark blue form as the water bearing clouds, seated on the top.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dhyānam te śīlayeyaṃ samatanusukhabaddhāsano nāsikāgra-
-nyastākṣaḥ pūrakādyairjitapavanapathaścittapadmaṃ tvavāñcam |
ūrdhvāgraṃ bhāvayitvā ravividhuśikhinaḥ saṃvicintyopariṣṭāt
tatrasthaṃ bhāvaye tvāṃ sajalajaladharaśyāmalaṃ komalāṅgam || 95-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आनीलश्लक्ष्णकेशं ज्वलितमकरसत्कुण्डलं मन्दहास-
-स्यन्दार्द्रं कौस्तुभश्रीपरिगतवनमालोरुहाराभिरामम् ।
श्रीवत्साङ्कं सुबाहुं मृदुलसदुदरं काञ्चनच्छायचेलं
चारुस्निग्धोरुमम्भोरुहललितपदं भावयेऽहं भवन्तम् ॥ ९५-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhattathiri meditates on Bhagwan’s blue form with lustrous hair, shining fish shaped earrings, a gentle smile with compassion flowing, lustre of Kaustubha spreading over the garlands and the big pearl necklaces, the Shreevatsa mark, a soft and charming abdomen, golden hued garment, well shaped thighs and lotus like tender feet.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ānīlaślakṣṇakeśaṃ jvalitamakarasatkuṇḍalaṃ mandahāsa-
-syandārdraṃ kaustubhaśrīparigatavanamāloruhārābhirāmam |
śrīvatsāṅkaṃ subāhuṃ mṛdulasadudaraṃ kāñcanacchāyacelaṃ
cārusnigdhorumambhoruhalalitaṃ padaṃ bhāvaye’haṃ bhavantam || 95-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सर्वाङ्गेष्वङ्ग रङ्गत्कुतुकमिति मुहुर्धारयन्नीश चित्तं
तत्राप्येकत्र युञ्जे वदनसरसिजे सुन्दरे मन्दहासे ।
तत्रालीनं तु चेतः परमसुखचिदद्वैतरूपे वितन्व-
-न्नन्यन्नो चिन्तयेयं मुहुरिति समुपारूढयोगो भवेयम् ॥ ९५-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Again and again Bhattathiri wants to concentrate with growing eagerness on every part of Bhagwan’s body and finally fix his mind on Bhagwan’s lotus like face with a gentle smile. The fully absorbed mind in the Eternal Bliss Consciousness in a non-dual form which will not think of anything else. Thus he shall remain steady in the advanced state of meditation, by repeated effort.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sarvāṅgeṣvaṅga raṅgatkutukamiti muhurdhārayannīśa cittaṃ
tatrāpyekatra yuñje vadanasarasije sundare mandahāse |
tatrālīnaṃ tu cetaḥ paramasukhacidadvaitarūpe vitanva-
-nanyanno cintayeyaṃ muhuriti samupārūḍhayogo bhaveyam || 95-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
इत्थं त्वद्ध्यानयोगे सति पुनरणिमाद्यष्टसंसिद्धयस्ताः
दूरश्रुत्यादयोऽपि ह्यहमहमिकया सम्पतेयुर्मुरारे ।
त्वत्सम्प्राप्तौ विलम्बावहमखिलमिदं नाद्रिये कामयेऽहं
त्वामेवानन्दपूर्णं पवनपुरपते पाहि मां सर्वतापात् ॥ ९५-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: When one practices such a Dhyana yoga, the benefits attainable are manifold. Even though all the siddhis would come to Bhattathiri, still he did not wanted these siddhis which would eventually come in way of contemplating on Bhagwan. Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan to bless him with the mind which is always fixed on HIM and requested to protect from all his afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
itthaṃ tvaddhyānayoge sati punaraṇimādyaṣṭasaṃsiddhayastāḥ
dūraśrutyādayo’pi hyahamahamikayā sampateyurmurāre |
tvatsamprāptau vilambāvahamakhilamidaṃ nādriye kāmaye’haṃ
tvāmevānandapūrṇaṃ pavanapurapate pāhi māṃ sarvatāpāt || 95-10 ||
